class_name: 自然発生-強制-ナイデハオカナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.canonical_surface: ないでなんかいられない
patterns.usage_note: Describes a reaction the subject is unable to suppress, almost always the speaker's own feeling or an act driven by it; the ずに variants are the everyday shape (する becomes せずにはいられない) and the ないでは variants are a little heavier, while the なんか・など・だって insertions add exasperation. Contrast the sibling ないではおかない, which is about what an event inevitably forces on someone else rather than what the speaker cannot resist.

examples.ruby: その手紙[てがみ]を読[よ]んで、涙[なみだ]をこぼさずにはいられなかった。
examples.english: Reading that letter, I just couldn't hold back the tears.

examples.ruby: 友[とも]だちが困[こま]っているのに、助[たす]けないでなんかいられないよ。
examples.english: My friend's having a hard time; there's no way I could just not help.

examples.ruby: 連絡[れんらく]が途絶[とだ]えたままなので、心配[しんぱい]せずにはいられません。
examples.english: With no word from them at all, I can't help worrying.

patterns.usage_note: Two readings share one form: with an event or a causative verb as subject, the thing inevitably provokes the result (この結末は読者を泣かせずにはおかない); with a human subject it is a hard vow not to let the matter rest. This is formal, written Japanese — commentary, criticism, courtroom-flavored prose — rather than conversation, and する becomes せずにはおかない. Where ずにはいられない reports a feeling the speaker cannot suppress, this pattern points outward at what will be inflicted or forced.

examples.ruby: この判決[はんけつ]は社会[しゃかい]に大[おお]きな議論[ぎろん]を呼[よ]ばずにはおかない。
examples.english: This ruling is bound to touch off a major debate in society.

examples.ruby: この物語[ものがたり]の結末[けつまつ]は、読[よ]む者[もの]の心[こころ]を捉[とら]えないではおかない。
examples.english: The ending of this tale cannot fail to seize the reader's heart.

examples.ruby: 我々[われわれ]は不正[ふせい]の全容[ぜんよう]を明[あき]らかにせずにはおかない。
examples.english: We will not rest until the full extent of the misconduct is laid bare.
